description.text:
The promos of Japan's Diamond & Pearl years: 127 cards, 001/DP-P to 127/DP-P, released from late 2006 to January 2009. The run began alongside Space-Time Creation, the first DP expansion, when the promo suffix changed from PCG-P to DP-P, and most of its cards are reprints of expansion cards.

The biggest groups came with Meiji Chocolate and from the Trade Please DP trading events at Pokémon Centers and the World Hobby Fair. Others came in each expansion's Special Pack and Official Visual Book, with McDonald's and Domino's Pizza, as Pokémon anniversary commemorative cards, through the Collection Challenge campaign, and at Battle Road, the Winter Challenge and the tournament that chose Japan's World Championships players.

Given to every player of Battle Road Stadium DP, the main card tournament of the Pokémon Diamond & Pearl Battle Festa 2006, which toured four venues in the Kansai, Tokai, Kyushu and Kanto regions between 25 November and 17 December 2006 to celebrate the new Diamond & Pearl games and cards. Came with the Pokémon Card Game DP Official Visual Book, which Media Factory published on 8 December 2006. description.text:
One of eight promos from the Trade Please DP corner (とりかえっこDP) of the 25th Next Generation World Hobby Fair, which visited Osaka on 14 January, Tokyo on 20 and 21 January, Nagoya on 28 January and Fukuoka on 4 February 2007. Visitors swapped one Pokémon card of their own, even an old yellow-bordered card or one with the old card back, for one of the eight, Turtwig, Chimchar, Piplup, Pachirisu, Buneary, Mime Jr., Glameow and Staravia, without choosing which, while stocks lasted. Trainer and Energy cards could not be swapped.

Official gym events in January and February 2007 ran the same corner and gave the same cards in their knockout battles and lotteries. The eight came back at the Gym Challenge tournaments held to launch the Secret of the Lakes expansion and the Rampardos and Bastiodon half decks, played with 30-card decks: every player got three cards for a first match, two for a second and three for a third, win or lose. This one came with the first match. Masakazu Fukuda drew it.

description.text:

All seven show Pokémon new to Diamond & Pearl: Turtwig, Chimchar, Piplup, Palkia, Drifblim, Croagunk and Dialga. It has the McDonald's M logo in its bottom left corner. Its attacks are those of Turtwig 017/DP-P from the Trade Please DP corner, with a new illustration. Masakazu Fukuda drew it.

The Movie 10th Anniversary Premium Sheet, eleven holo cards of the stars of the Pokémon films so far, sold at cinemas and Pokémon Centers from the same day, had a pocket for this card. Kouki Saitou drew it.

description.text:
A holo card for children who took the First Classroom DP (はじめて教室DP) at the Winter Challenge, a free event at eight venues across Japan on eleven days from 25 November 2007 to 20 January 2008. description.text:
One of three holo cards, Gible, Gabite and Garchomp, in the participation pack of the first stage of the Pokémon World Championships Japan Representative Tournament (ポケモンワールドチャンピオンシップス日本代表決定大会), which chose Japan's players for the 2009 World Championships. Announced as the next official tournament after Battle Road Spring 2008 was cut short, it brought video game and card game players to the same venues. The first stage visited all 47 prefectures, from Hyogo on 12 October 2008 to Tokyo B on 25 January 2009, and its card game rounds were played with 30-card half decks. Players pre-registered as Pokémon Daisuki Club members and were picked by lottery.

Gible is numbered 097/DP-P and its evolutions 103 and 104, with the five Pokémon Center 10th anniversary Pikachus between them. Hiroki Fuchino drew it.

description.text:
Given to cinema-goers at the release of Giratina and the Sky's Bouquet: Shaymin (ギラティナと氷空の花束 シェイミ), the 2008 Pokémon film, which opened across Japan on 19 July 2008. The first 4 million viewers got this card, while stocks lasted, with a Pokémon Battrio Special Pack of Shaymin and a Shaymin thank-you sticker. It shows Giratina in its Another Forme, as it appears in the real world, and its attack Dragon Breath (りゅうのいぶき) ties in with the film.

It is one of the 13 cards of the Collection Challenge (コレクションチャレンジ), Pokémon Card Game's big campaign of summer 2008, which from 10 July handed out original cards at cinemas showing the new Pokémon film, card and game shops, events and other places across Japan, a different Pokémon at each. Their illustrations and attacks were made for the campaign, and Midori Harada drew eleven of the thirteen.

Members of the free Pokémon Daisuki Club fan club could also collect the cards in a mini-game on its website until 1 September 2008; 300 of those who collected nine won, by draw, a set of the twelve cards given out at shops and events, all but Real World's Giratina.

Kagemaru Himeno drew it.

Given to children who finished one of the Pokémon stamp rallies run with railways in the summer of 2008: JR East's around Tokyo, from 26 July to 10 August, where finishers took their rally stamp book to Pokémon Center Tokyo or Yokohama; JR Hokkaido's, from 30 July to 10 August at the Pokémon Center in Sapporo Esta and the rally's goal counter at Sapporo Station; JR West's, from 8 to 24 August, at Pokémon Center Osaka and Kyoto, Tennoji and Sannomiya stations; and Meitetsu's bingo rally along its lines, from 19 July to 31 August, for completing one vertical line of the bingo card.

Six of the cards, Turtwig, Chimchar, Piplup, Buizel, Pachirisu and Croagunk, form a ring: each has an attack that grows stronger when the next is in play, and Croagunk's leads back to Turtwig. Turtwig's Hot Hot (あっちっち) adds 20 damage and burns the opponent when Chimchar is in play.

It is one of the 13 cards of the Collection Challenge (コレクションチャレンジ), Pokémon Card Game's big campaign of summer 2008, which from 10 July handed out original cards at cinemas showing the new Pokémon film, card and game shops, events and other places across Japan, a different Pokémon at each. Their illustrations and attacks were made for the campaign, and Midori Harada drew eleven of the thirteen.

Members of the free Pokémon Daisuki Club fan club could also collect the cards in a mini-game on its website until 1 September 2008; 300 of those who collected nine won, by draw, a set of the twelve cards given out at shops and events, all but Real World's Giratina.

Midori Harada drew it.

description.text:
The second Pokémon Center 10th anniversary card. To mark ten years since the Pokémon Centers opened, all five stores, Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya, Fukuoka and Yokohama, gave it to each shopper from 22 August to 7 September 2008, while stocks lasted. Its attack Little Errand (ちいさなおつかい) finds a basic Energy card in the deck, much as the Pikachus' Shopping finds a Pokémon Tool.

Pikachu came first, from 30 May 2008, in a slightly different version at each store (098 to 102/DP-P). Squirtle 009/DPt-P, picked by a vote over Meowth, followed from 14 November 2008 and Bulbasaur 030/DPt-P from 4 April 2009, when shoppers who brought any two of the four got a Pokémon Card Game coin. Yuka Morii made it.
